General.Description:
The Esperanza sank off the coast of Hispaniola in 1671 with a cargo manifest that listed, among other things, forty-three wooden crates described only as "ecclesiastical materials." Maritime historians have argued about those crates for three hundred and fifty years. Marine archaeologist Rowan Ash thinks she knows what was in them. She also thinks she knows exactly where the Esperanza is.

Proving it requires funding she does not have, equipment she cannot afford, and permission from the Dominican government to excavate a site within a protected marine area. It also requires surviving the attentions of a private salvage operation that has been working the same coordinates for two years and has no interest in sharing the find with an academic who believes the contents of those crates belong to no individual and every museum.

The Wreck of the Esperanza is a tightly plotted underwater adventure that combines the methodical excitement of marine archaeology with the propulsive tension of a race against well-resourced opponents. Isla McKenzie writes dive sequences with an immediacy that puts the reader in the water alongside her protagonist, and her portrait of the ethical debates around cultural heritage and salvage rights gives the action genuine moral stakes.

Absorbing and beautifully paced.
